fact: A spiral galaxy in Cetus, about 50 million light-years away, with a brilliant active nucleus.
bio: Pierre Méchain discovered it in 1780. M77, also known as NGC 1068, is a Seyfert galaxy: its centre is intensely bright, powered by a supermassive black hole. In 1985 Antonucci and Miller found broad emission lines hidden in its polarised light and argued that a dusty torus hides the central engine from some viewing angles, a finding that supported the unified model of active galaxies. A small telescope shows it.
